text:
anna: heads-up — observed a p95 spike (~220ms -> ~480ms) today tied to the CUTLASS fallback handoff. Happened across a ~6m window, esp. for requests with seqlen in the 50-120 bucket. traces: https://infralogs/replay/abc123 :eye:
josh: thx. any correlation with KV-cache misses or batching windows?

maria: quick dump from the profiler (sampled during the window):
```
model: redwood-v1
hw: h100
seqlen: 64-96 (bulk)
triton path p95: 180ms
cutlass path p95: 210ms
cutlass fallback path p95 (post-routing): 470ms
observed handoffs: 1.8% of requests
avg batch size (fallback): 2.1
kv-miss-rate (fallback): 12%
```

eli: that 12% KV miss rate is suspicious — could be cold-prefixes hitting fallback execution which then forces smaller batches and triggers worse kernel selection. Did the probe-sampler rate change?

anna: we rolled a small routing tweak at 08:48 (canary) — deploy-bot shows: deploy-bot: "canary routing/arbiter v3.2.1 -> v3.2.2 applied to 5%". Putting that here — probably the trigger.

josh: can you paste the handoff policy we shipped? I want to see thresholds + hysteresis.

maria: snippet from config we shipped:
```
# routing arbiter v3.2.2
handoff_threshold: 0.8
handoff_min_dwell_s: 30
probe_sample_rate: 0.02
fallback_backoff: 0.5  # multiplier for quick retries
```

eli: two quick notes: (1) dwell=30s + sample_rate=2% can be noisy when traffic mixes seqlens; (2) fallback_backoff=0.5 might be too aggressive causing flip-flopping if a single sample looks bad. We should add a smoothing window for the measured p95 and require N consecutive bad probes before handoff.

anna: agreed. i'm thinking: increase handoff_threshold to 0.86 for the cluster, + require 3 bad probes in a 2m sliding window before switching. Also bump min_dwell to 60s. Quick experiment?

maria: ok running a small sim against the trace replay. command: `./tools/replay --trace abc123 --arbiter-config experiments/handshake-a.json`

maria: sim results (30m replay, seeded traffic):
```
baseline (v3.2.1): global p95 = 195ms
canary (v3.2.2 original): global p95 = 237ms (+21%)
candidate (threshold=0.86, dwell=60s, require=3): global p95 = 198ms (+1.5%)
handoff_count baseline: 420
handoff_count canary: 1980
handoff_count candidate: 630
```

josh: that looks promising — reduced noisy handoffs and p95 back near baseline. Any side-effects on throughput?

maria: throughput stable. batch sizes for fallback requests increased from 2.1 -> 3.6 on candidate. KV miss pattern unchanged.

eli: sounds like signal smoothing plus higher threshold reduces oscillation. We should also add a metric for `arbiter.handoff_spike` and an alert on >1.5x baseline in a 5m window.

anna: action items: 1) roll candidate config to 20% canary, 2) add handoff_spike metric + alert, 3) increase probe sampling for seqlen 50-128 to 3% for better signal, 4) add docs note about dwell/hysteresis rationale. I'll open a PR for the config and the alert.

josh: i'll own the canary rollout and watch p50/p95 + handoff_count, will post updates. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: "canary rollout triggered: routing/arbiter v3.2.2-candidate at 20%"

anna: thanks all. if you see any other clusters with similar signature ping here.
